 Beyond the Recall Notice: Why Pharmacies Need Greater Visibility Into Recalled and Expired Medications
 Oct 19, 2026 8:00am 
 Health Tech 
 -->
 Medication recalls and expirations are a routine part of pharmacy operations, but managing them often requires significant time, coordination and attention to detail. Pharmacy teams may need to review recall notices, verify lot information, search inventory, document actions taken and coordinate returns, all while managing prescription volume, patient needs and an expanding set of clinical responsibilities. 
 The challenge is not a lack of awareness. Pharmacy teams understand the importance of identifying recalled and expired medications and removing them from inventory. The challenge is doing so quickly, consistently and with confidence while balancing the growing demands of modern pharmacy practice.
 As pharmacies continue to evolve beyond traditional dispensing roles, operational visibility is becoming increasingly important. Supporting medication safety requires more than knowing a recall has occurred. It requires the ability to understand where products are located, how they have moved through pharmacy workflows and what actions may need to be taken next.
 The Hidden Complexity Behind Medication Management 
 When a recall is issued, pharmacies must determine whether affected products are in inventory and, in some cases, whether those products have moved further along the dispensing process. Teams may need to verify lot information, locate products and document actions taken to support compliance requirements.
 Expired medication management presents a similar challenge. Products must be identified before they can be removed from active inventory and processed through appropriate return channels. For organizations managing large inventories or multiple locations, these activities can require significant coordination across teams and systems.
 The challenge becomes even greater when recall notices, inventory data and return workflows reside in separate systems. Staff often need to move between platforms to gather information, confirm product status and document next steps Each additional step introduces complexity and creates opportunities for delays.
 For pharmacy leaders, the issue is not simply operational efficiency. It is about maintaining visibility, reliability and control across the medication lifecycle while enabling pharmacy teams to remain focused on patient care.
 Why Serialization Matters 
 As pharmacies navigate evolving traceability and compliance expectations, including those associated with the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA), serialized inventory data is becoming an increasingly important tool for understanding product movement and inventory status. 
 Traditionally, recall management has centered on identifying affected products at a broad inventory level. Serialization introduces a more precise approach by associating medications with unique product identifiers that can help support tracking, tracing and responsible data sharing across applicable supply chain activities.
 This added visibility can support recall investigations, return processing and documentation activities. While serialization does not replace professional judgment, it can give pharmacy teams more complete information when determining how to respond to recalls and expirations.
 For pharmacy leaders, serialization can strengthen inventory management by supporting more informed decisions when recalls and expirations occur.
 Connecting Recall Management, Traceability and Reverse Logistics 
 As pharmacies modernize their operations, many organizations are looking for ways to connect the systems and processes involved in managing recalled and expired medications.
 Supplylogix® Reverse Logistics brings recall management and expired medication returns together within a connected reverse logistics framework. Integrated with the EnterpriseRx® pharmacy management system, the solution is designed to provide pharmacies with a consolidated view of potential exposure across inventory, dispensing and patient information. 
 By connecting these workflows, pharmacy teams can more efficiently identify potentially affected products, support documentation for compliance and reporting and help reduce the need to navigate between separate systems. The solution can also help identify products approaching expiration before manufacturer return cutoffs are missed, supporting more timely return decisions and helping reduce avoidable product waste.
 Serialization plays an important role in this approach. When combined with pharmacy management information, serialized inventory data can provide greater insight into product movement and inventory status, supporting coordinated decisions throughout the medication lifecycle.
 A More Connected Future for Pharmacy Operations 
 Managing recalled and expired medications will always require human oversight, professional judgment and decisive action from pharmacy teams. However, the tools supporting those decisions continue to evolve.
 For pharmacy leaders, the goal is not simply to respond more quickly when a recall occurs. It is to create an operating environment that gives teams the information and coordination needed to act with confidence. 
 As pharmacies continue expanding their role in patient care, bringing together pharmacy management information, serialized inventory data and reverse logistics processes may become increasingly important. In an environment where patient safety and operational efficiency increasingly intersect, a clearer view of the medication journey can help organizations navigate complexity with greater confidence while keeping patients’ needs at the center.
